programme.title: The Age of Uncertainty
programme.desc: Prof JK Galbraith sets out his personal view of democracy, comparing politics in Switzerland, Britain and the US and emphasising Nehru's influence in India.

programme.title: Fred Dibnah's Age of Steam
programme.desc: Fred explores how steam power lives on in the modern age through the steam turbine and its critical role in electricity generation. In addition, Fred also looks at how the history of steam is being preserved through heritage museums.

programme.title: Pubs, Ponds, and Power: The Story of the Village
programme.desc: Archaeologist Ben Robinson discovers the story of Cromford, a picturesque Derbyshire village at the heart of famous industrialist Sir Richard Arkwright's mechanised cotton mills and a textile revolution. Cromford became a new kind of village, built to service the enterprise of this powerful man.

programme.title: Matthew Bourne's Sleeping Beauty

programme.title: Clive James
programme.desc: Clive James travels to the eternal city in search of the dolce vita and to acquire some Roman sophistication. During his stay, he meets a socialite prince, Mussolini's son and learns a lesson from a sexologist.

programme.title: The Morecambe and Wise Show
programme.desc: A complete episode of The Morecambe and Wise Show, that had been considered lost for over 50 years. Eric's son Gary Morecambe discovered the programme in an unmarked film can, and now it has been lovely restored and can be enjoyed in full for the first time since being broadcast on October 8th 1970.

programme.title: The Perfect Morecambe & Wise
programme.desc: Eric takes on the demanding role of Hamlet, the boys re-enact `Singing In The Rain', Dame Flora Robson revives her role as the virgin queen and Cilla Black has some great news for Ernie about his recording career.

programme.title: The Black Swan

programme.title: The Black Swan

programme.title: Winter Walks
programme.desc: The picture-perfect setting of Cumbria's Dentdale is the location for Lemn Sissay's breathtaking journey into a world of snow-capped hills, blue skies and birdsong. Starting high on the moorlands above Dent village, and carrying a 360-degree camera, Lemn walks along ancient drovers' roads and the old postman's path, with breathtaking winter views in every direction. Meeting locals, including a farmer who collects vintage tractors and a lone bagpiper, Lemn is inspired.

programme.title: Christmas University Challenge
programme.sub-title: University College, Oxford v University of Glasgow
programme.desc: Teams of alumni from University College, Oxford face off against the University of Glasgow. Broadcaster Paul Gambaccini captains the University College team, while author Christopher Brookmyre leads Glasgow. Jeremy Paxman asks the questions.

programme.title: Concorde: A Supersonic Story
programme.desc: The life of the most glamorous plane ever built, told by the people whose lives she touched. On the eve of the opening of Bristol's aerospace museum, a cast of engineers, flight technicians and frequent fliers tell the supersonic story.

programme.title: Being the Brontës
programme.desc: To mark the 200th anniversary of Charlotte Brontë's birth, Martha Kearney, novelist Helen Oyeyemi and journalist Lucy Mangan travel to Haworth Parsonage, the home of Charlotte and her sisters Emily and Anne, to discover the inspiration behind their classic novels `Jane Eyre', `Wuthering Heights' and `Agnes Grey'. The trio learn how the Brontës combined literary genius with real life experience to create some of the best-loved novels in the English language.

programme.title: Kay Adshead Remembers: Wuthering Heights
programme.desc: Actor, producer and writer Kay Adshead reflects on her memorable portrayal of Cathy Earnshaw in the BBC's 1978 adaptation of Wuthering Heights. She recalls the intensity of filming on the Yorkshire moors, working alongside Ken Hutchison.

programme.title: Wuthering Heights
